known_open_bug_before_holdout.description: nflprops.project._roster() showed Tua Tagovailoa on ATL for 2026 W3. Decision #31 flagged this as a suspected data bug (assumed MIA); decision #34 'fixed' it as a data correction to MIA. Decision #35 (2026-09-24) reverted #34: Sean confirmed Tua genuinely moved to Atlanta in 2026. The upstream nflreadpy roster value was correct all along -- there was never a roster-pipeline bug. _roster(), ingest.py's team-mapping, and the rosters table all reflect ATL, which is right.
known_open_bug_before_holdout.status: closed, decision #35 (2026-09-24) -- false positive, no bug existed. The real risk this surfaced was in nflprops/reliability.py's star_pool(): a player who switches teams and hasn't played yet can still outrank the actual current starter, because usage was ranked on career history regardless of how stale it is. Fixed generally in decision #35 -- star_pool() now zeroes usage for any player flagged changed_team by role_continuity() who also has zero games this season, so an unconfirmed role can't outrank someone actually on the field. reliability.py is not in this manifest's code_sha256 (it sits outside the locked engine, same as ingest.py), so the engine lock and this file's hashes are unaffected; engine/check_drift.py still passes.
known_open_bug_before_holdout.must_fix_before: N/A -- there was nothing to fix before the holdout opens; this entry stays for the record
